questionsToConsider: What is the minimum age, and which countries or regions can legally enter where you run this?
Is one entry per person the rule, or do referrals earn extra entries?
Is the prize something you post, hand over in person or send digitally, and do you offer a voucher alternative?
Where do your official rules live, and does the consent text link to them clearly?
guide.howToUseResponses: Before the draw, export entries to CSV and remove duplicates by email, then check every remaining entrant's country against your rules. Pick the winner at random from the cleaned list and keep a copy of it in case anyone asks how the draw was run. Only add people who said yes to the newsletter to your mailing list, and use the heard-about answers to see which channel brought in the most entries for next time.
customizeSteps: Name the prize in the greeting, and change the delivery options to the ways you can actually hand it over, or delete that question if there is only one.
Change the age question and the consent text to match your official rules, and add a link to the full rules in the consent wording.
Put the closing date in the greeting, then share the link in your posts or embed it on a landing page.

faqs.q: What should a giveaway entry form include?
faqs.a: An eligibility check, contact details to reach the winner, a location if the giveaway is limited by region, and agreement to the official rules. Keep marketing opt-ins separate and optional.

faqs.q: Can I require people to join my newsletter to enter?
faqs.a: Privacy laws such as the GDPR expect marketing consent to be freely given, so it is safer to make the newsletter a separate, optional choice. This form asks it as its own question and says the answer won't affect the entry.

faqs.q: How do I stop people entering more than once?
faqs.a: State one entry per person in the rules, then remove duplicate emails before the draw. The consent line in this form also has entrants confirm they are entering once.

faqs.q: How do I pick a winner fairly?
faqs.a: Export the eligible entries, number them, and use a random number generator to pick one. Keep the list and the result in case you need to show how it was done.

doc.title: Giveaway entry
doc.description: A short, fair entry path that checks eligibility first and records rule acceptance.

blocks.title: You're a couple of minutes away from being entered. Let's check you're eligible first.
Where should we contact you if you win?
Which country and city do you live in?
blocks.description: The rules say where the giveaway is open, and we check before announcing a winner.

blocks.title: If you win, how would you like to receive the prize?
blocks.description: We'll confirm the details with the winner before anything is sent.

blocks.title: How did you hear about the giveaway?
In a sentence or two, what would winning mean to you?
blocks.description: Optional, and it has no effect on who wins. The draw is random.

blocks.title: Would you also like our newsletter? Saying no won't affect your entry.
Official rules
blocks.consentText: I have read the official giveaway rules, I am entering once, and I understand the winner is picked at random from eligible entries and contacted by email.

endings.title: You're entered 🎉
endings.bodyMd: Good luck! We'll pick a winner after the closing date and contact them by email, so check your spam folder around then.

endings.title: Sorry, this one is 18+
endings.bodyMd: This giveaway is only open to adults, so we haven't recorded an entry. Thanks for your interest, and keep an eye out for future ones.

closeRules.closedMessageMd: This form is no longer accepting responses.
